Outside the list, the `do:` rule lost "A `for` always takes `do ... end`" and One expression per line gained "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line"; that sentence is why haiku-1 line 156 (limit_rows = for {user, limit} <- limits, do: {{:limit, user}, limit}) is not listed, where the previous text would have listed it. The macros.md changes do not reach this case.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 1 of 5 (sonnet-1), a judgment call. Its init/1 with (line 151) is the allowed one-step form and its load_limits/1 chains two steps, so nothing in the case's check is broken. What breaks is "Give each step a private function that returns `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}`": read_file/1, decode_json/1 and parse_limits/1 return {:stop, ...} (lines 182, 192, 201, 205) so that the tuple falls straight out of init/1. I held it violated because the sentence is literal and 2026-10-22-check-7 cited the same helpers under this rule, though there the deciding point was a one-step with that the rule then forbade. Reading the sentence as the usual shape and not a limit makes sonnet-1 clean, the count 0 of 5 and the sonnet tier clean. Opus-1 and sonnet-2 chain two steps ending in a tail call; haiku-1 and haiku-2 read with raising boot-time calls and are not exercised. Sonnet-2's init/1 else (line 122) only rewraps the reason for init/1, not counted as in 2026-10-21-check-2 and 2026-10-22. Its moduledoc controller with (lines 38-51) has two steps and two else clauses, one per error shape, each producing a response; it is not the large else the rule names, so it is not counted.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call: 0 of 5, one judgment. Haiku-2 lines 108-114 spread the ETS options inside :ets.new/2, a list that mixes atoms and keywords. The case's check says "a keyword list that is the call's last argument, such as the ETS table options, may stay inline, one option per line", and the one-line form is 106 characters, so "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." does not reach it. Reading the mixed list as not a keyword list makes haiku-2 violated and the count 1 of 5. Haiku-1's @table_options (lines 60-66) is 103 characters on one line, so it is clean too. Last sweep's one violation has no counterpart: no run spreads a list that fits its line.

Comments: 0 of 5. The close call is sonnet-2 line 190 (# Returns the rows to store: the default limit and one row per listed user.). Held clean because the 2026-10-31 baseline grade held the same kind of one-line description above a defp clean (sonnet-1 line 106), and because parse_limits does not say its result is table rows. The 2026-10-23 grade held a comment that restated the Enum.filter/2 under it violated; following that reading makes sonnet-2 violated and the count 1 of 5.

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition is clean; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict (all five; opus-1 gives the reason in a comment at lines 190-191); a run with no with and only raising boot-time calls is not exercised under the with rule; placeholder comments inside @moduledoc examples are not counted (opus-1 line 106); callers and child lists in @moduledoc count as the run's caller and supervision examples; key, row, config and decoded are not counted under Naming; a one-expression body written as a block (such as haiku-1 lines 140-142 or haiku-2 lines 130-132) is not counted under the `do:` rule; Keyword.get/3 in place of Keyword.validate!/2 and a start_link/1 with no @spec are not counted. Group related parameters is listed for sonnet-1 as 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 listed the same shape.

Designs. All five keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer that accepts :name and gives the table that name; the caller inserts, counts with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes its row when over; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes expired rows with :ets.select_delete/2. No run has handle_call/3 or cast, and no run calls Jason. Limits live in :persistent_term (opus-1), as one row per user in the same table (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2) or as one row holding the whole limits struct (sonnet-1), which copies the map on every check. Last sweep's Code.eval_file/1 design and missing :name option did not recur.

Verification, in scratch copies under grade-scratch-b/rate-limiter-skill (Elixir 1.20.3, OTP 29). All five pass mix format --check-formatted, have no line over 98 characters and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. No run ever admitted more than its limit. Across 300 bursts of 50 tasks released together at limit 2, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 admitted exactly 2 each time; opus-1 admitted 2 in 281, 1 in 18 and 0 in 1, and 4 of 5 in one burst at limit 5, under-admission its @doc warns of at lines 165-166. In 500 bursts of 8 first requests at limit 1, no run admitted more than 1, and bursts that admitted none numbered 25 in opus-1 and 1 to 7 in the others; sonnet-2 crashed 92 of 4,000 calls with Enum.EmptyError, because retry_after/3 (line 150) runs after the caller deleted its own row (line 106), and Enum.min/1 gets an empty list when every racing row is gone; no rule on the list covers it. Opus-1 avoids the same crash by reading before it deletes (lines 215-217). A second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50 in all five. An injected 61-second-old row was removed by one :sweep message and the live and limit rows kept, in all five. Opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 convert IDs with to_string/1, so 42 and "42" share a count; sonnet-1 accepts only binaries.
